xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5238: Skills for this issue takes 37-77 s to load (GET /api/skills/overrides?issue=)

plan.title: Skills for this issue takes 37-77 s to load (GET /api/skills/overrides?issue=)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: GET /api/skills/overrides makes about 3,900 fs/promises calls per request, and nearly all of them are awaited one at a time: 475 SKILL.md reads in listSkillCatalog, plus 3,408 lstat/readdir calls in listPackCatalog -> readPackManifest -> listExecutables. Each call queues on libuv's 4-thread pool. While the dashboard keeps that pool busy (121 MB parseTranscriptSnapshot reads, cost sweeps), the real functions took 66 s under synthetic saturation (26.0 s + 40.5 s), consistent with the report, against 0.5 s on a quiet pool. The issue's suspect, resolveProjectFromIssueSync, is mtime-cached and is not the cause. The slow window was not reproduced live; it fell in the first minutes after a dashboard restart.
narratives.Proposal: Shorten the sequential chain. (1) listSkillCatalog reads roots and SKILL.md files concurrently through a 32-slot fs limiter (createPromiseConcurrencyLimiter), keeping first-root-wins precedence. (2) listPackCatalog reuses a pack manifest while its extract dir keeps the same inode, mtime, ctime, adapter and read options. (3) readPackManifest reads SKILL.md files and walks executables concurrently through a 32-slot limiter, with identical output order. (4) projectForIssue switches to the async resolver for rule compliance. (5) The GET route logs a slow line at 2000 ms or more as the fallback diagnostic. (6) docs/SKILL-PACKS.md and changelog.d/pan-5238.md describe the change.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Changing UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE or the dashboard launcher environment
- Fixing what congests the threadpool (parseTranscriptSnapshot of 121 MB files, costReconcileSweep)
- Any frontend change to SkillOverridesPanel or IssueSkillsSection
- Caching the native skill catalog (~/.overdeck/skills, ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills, <project>/.pan/skills)
- Changing listLowerLevelOverrides or listLowerLevelPackOverrides
- Per-phase timing inside listSkillStates or any change to its signature
- Any change to the response shape of GET or PUT /api/skills/overrides
- Unbounded Promise.all over fs calls (every fs fan-out goes through a 32-slot limiter)
- Invalidation hooks in updatePack/removePack/enablePackBrowser/disablePackBrowser (the inode+mtime stamp covers rebuilds)

autoDecisions.summary: Fix the measured mechanism (a sequential fs chain under threadpool load) rather than only the issue's suspected sync lookup.
autoDecisions.rationale: Planning measured resolveProjectFromIssueSync as mtime-cached (one statSync), counted about 3,900 serial fs calls per request, and reproduced 66 s for the real catalog functions with a saturated threadpool against 0.5 s on a quiet one.

autoDecisions.summary: Ship a slow-request log line on GET /api/skills/overrides as the fallback diagnostic.
autoDecisions.rationale: The 37-77 s window could not be reproduced live (every request now takes 0.26-3.3 s), and dashboard.log has no timestamps, so the next occurrence must leave evidence.

autoDecisions.summary: Bound every fs fan-out at 32 in-flight tasks through the existing createPromiseConcurrencyLimiter, wrapping leaf fs calls only.
autoDecisions.rationale: Measured 466 reads under load: 24.2 s sequential, 1.5 s at 16, 0.73 s at 32, 0.45 s at 64. 32 keeps most of the gain while capping one request's share of the 4-thread pool queue; wrapping a recursive walk in a shared limiter can deadlock.

autoDecisions.summary: Key the pack-manifest cache on extract-dir inode + mtime + ctime + adapter + read options, with no invalidation hooks.
autoDecisions.rationale: extractCommit renames a freshly built temp dir into place on every rebuild. Its rm runs before its mkdir, so ext4 may reuse the inode number, but mtime and ctime still change. The browser flag lives inside the read options.

autoDecisions.summary: Swap projectForIssue to the async resolveProjectFromIssue as its own small item, traced to NFR-2 rather than to the performance FR.
autoDecisions.rationale: src/lib/projects.ts forbids sync callers in server-reachable code, and the swap is cheap, but it is not the cause of the latency.

items.title: Read skill catalog roots and SKILL.md files concurrently through a 32-slot limiter

expected_outputs: catalog.test.ts passes the precedence case and the concurrency case

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-1 exactly. In src/lib/skill-overrides/catalog.ts, import createPromiseConcurrencyLimiter from '../concurrency.js', add const CATALOG_FS_CONCURRENCY = 32 and const limitFs = createPromiseConcurrencyLimiter(CATALOG_FS_CONCURRENCY). In readRoot, wrap readdir and each readFile in limitFs and map dirents through Promise.all, filtering out nulls (the PRD gives the before/after code). In listSkillCatalog, run readRoot for every root through Promise.all, then merge perRoot in root order with first-name-wins. Never wrap readRoot itself in limitFs. Create src/lib/skill-overrides/__tests__/catalog.test.ts with real temp dirs passed as home/projectRoot: a precedence case and a concurrency case that mocks node:fs/promises readFile to count peak in-flight calls over 40 skills.

items.title: Given dup under both <home>/.overdeck/skills and <home>/.claude/skills, when listSkillCatalog runs, then it returns dup with origin 'overdeck', returns a project-only skill with origin 'project' and projectSkill true, omits a dir without SKILL.md, and sorts by name
Given 40 skill dirs in one root and a node:fs/promises mock counting in-flight readFile calls, when listSkillCatalog runs, then the peak in-flight count is above 1 and at most 32
catalog.ts creates exactly one module-level limiter from CATALOG_FS_CONCURRENCY = 32, and limitFs wraps only readdir and readFile calls, never readRoot
Reuse a pack manifest while its extract dir keeps the same inode, mtime, ctime, adapter and read options

expected_outputs: catalog.test.ts passes the three pack-manifest-cache cases, and launch.test.ts and conversation-flags.test.ts pass

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-2 exactly. In src/lib/skill-overrides/catalog.ts, replace isDirectory with dirStats(path): Promise<Stats | null> (lstat result when it is a directory, else null; import type Stats from 'node:fs'). Add a module-level Map<string, { stamp: string; manifest: PackManifest }> named manifestCache. In listPackCatalog, build readOpts (optIn, skillsRoot, pluginRoot, browser === 'ready', skillsExclude) once, compute stamp = `${stats.ino}:${stats.mtimeMs}:${stats.ctimeMs}:${adapter}:${JSON.stringify(readOpts)}`, return the cached manifest on a stamp match, otherwise call readPackManifest(dir, adapter, readOpts) and store it. On a thrown read, set manifest = null and delete the entry. Keep the cached/browser/adapter computation running on every call, outside the cache. Update the module header comment. Add three cases to catalog.test.ts, mocking ../../skill-packs/sources.js (listPacks, packExtractDir, packRenderDir) and wrapping readPackManifest in vi.fn around the real one. manifestCache is module-level: every test case builds its own fresh mkdtempSync extract dir, and beforeEach calls vi.mocked(readPackManifest).mockClear(). Mock sources.js partially with importOriginal so its other exports stay real.

Walk pack executables and read pack SKILL.md files concurrently with identical output order

expected_outputs: adapters.test.ts passes unchanged, and adapters-concurrency.test.ts, gstack.test.ts and deft.test.ts pass

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-3 exactly. In src/lib/skill-packs/adapters.ts, import createPromiseConcurrencyLimiter from '../concurrency.js' and add MANIFEST_FS_CONCURRENCY = 32 and a module-level limitFs. Rewrite listExecutables so walk returns string[]: it wraps readdir and lstat in limitFs, maps the sorted dirents through Promise.all, and flattens, which keeps sorted DFS order. Never wrap walk or listExecutables in limitFs. In readPackManifest, read every SKILL.md with Promise.all(skillDirs.map(dir => limitFs(() => readTextOrNull(...)))), keep the existing ordered frontmatter/name/SKILL_NAME_PATTERN/seen logic over the results inside skillDirs.forEach, turning each `continue` into `return` (the PRD shows the full snippet), collect the kept non-gstack dirs, then run listExecutables on them through Promise.all and push the results in order. Leave scanSkillDirs and gstackSkillDirs unchanged. Do not edit the existing adapters.test.ts. Create adapters-concurrency.test.ts with the two cases from the PRD.

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-4. In src/lib/skill-overrides/issue-file.ts, import { Effect } from 'effect', replace resolveProjectFromIssueSync with resolveProjectFromIssue in the projects.js import, and in projectForIssue use `const resolved = await Effect.runPromise(resolveProjectFromIssue(issueId));`. This is the same pattern as src/dashboard/server/routes/fleet-work.ts. Run the five listed suites. If a suite fully mocks lib/projects.js with only resolveProjectFromIssueSync and now fails with 'No "resolveProjectFromIssue" export is defined on the mock', add resolveProjectFromIssue to that mock, returning Effect.succeed(<the same value>). In that case also add the test file to this item's commit. Never change production code to suit a mock.

Log a slow line for GET /api/skills/overrides at 2000 ms or more

expected_outputs: skill-overrides-route.test.ts passes, including the slow and fast logging cases

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-5. In src/dashboard/server/routes/misc/skill-overrides.ts, add const SLOW_REQUEST_MS = 2000. In getSkillOverridesRoute's Effect.promise body, take const started = Date.now() before skillStatesResponseBody. In a finally block, when Date.now() - started >= SLOW_REQUEST_MS, call console.warn with `[skill-overrides] slow GET level=<issue|project|global> project=<key|-> issue=<id|-> ms=<n>`. Use Date.now(), not performance.now(). The response is unchanged. Add two tests to skill-overrides-route.test.ts. The slow case uses vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] }), with a listSkillStates mock that calls vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 2500) before returning, and spies console.warn. Fake only Date, because faking setTimeout/setImmediate can stall the Effect scheduler. The fast case uses the default mock. Restore real timers in afterEach. Repo rule: delay tests use fake timers, never real waits.
